Matrix Major Actions

Action Types

Each action has a note next to it indicating when it can be performed; this is either Initiative (I) or Anytime (A).

Major Actions

These actions take a bit more concentration or time to complete. Several involve a test of some kind, but some simply occur as long as you have the Action available. Just like Minor Actions, if there is no test involved but the gamemaster feels the pressure is on and one should be required, they have final say in the matter.

Minor Actions

These actions usually take only a small amount of focus or a quick and simple thought or movement. A key point among Minor Actions is that they generally do not require a test of any kind. That doesn’t mean in truly dire situations where the pressure is on that the gamemaster can’t ask for a test to be made—it just means that usually, as long as you have the action available, you can perform the task by simply declaring the use of it.

Effects

Situational Modifiers

Gear

Effects and Modification Fields

The Modifications field on Effects, qualities, augmentations, gear, devices, programs, echoes, complex forms, adept powers, metamagics, vehicle programs and modifications, and other supported rows can change sheet values automatically. Effects apply only while their Active toggle is on. Programs and other powered items apply only while powered on. Newly added power-controlled rows begin disabled. Turning an entry off or removing it reverses its contribution.

The Statuses tab beside Effects maintains its own repeating list of standard or custom statuses. NPC sheets provide the same controls in a separate Statuses section. A preset creates a disabled row with its level or damage code, duration, source reference, rules description, and any standard Modifications. Review the row, then turn on its Active toggle when the status applies.

Active standard statuses also apply rules that cannot be represented by a simple numeric attribute change. These include roll, attack, defense, Attack Rating, Defense Rating, visibility, hearing, movement, Sprint, Edge, and action restrictions. Affected roll results identify the contributing status. Hobbled halves Move and the completed Sprint result; statuses that prevent an action suppress that action rather than merely reducing its pool.

Writing modifications

Enter each modification as modifier_name:value. Separate multiple modifications with commas. Positive and negative values are supported.

body_modifier:2, perception_modifier:-1, initiative_dice_mod:1

Modifiers from multiple active entries are cumulative. Use the exact names below; spaces in a modifier name are not supported.

On a repeating row with a Rating field, use rating_num as the value to apply that row’s current rating. For example, body_modifier:rating_num on an active Rating 3 gear item adds 3. Negative and multiplied forms such as body_modifier:-rating_num and body_modifier:rating_num*2 are also supported. Changing the row’s rating automatically adjusts the applied amount.

Manual Mod versus Effects Mod

For physical, mental, and AI attributes and skills, the combined positive bonus from Mod and Effects Mod is capped at +4. Magic and Resonance are exempt from this cap. An enabled temporary attribute bonus is included in the same +4 attribute cap where applicable. The entered values remain visible in their individual fields, but a capped attribute or skill uses no more than +4 total enhancement. Negative modifiers are not limited by this rule. Situational Skill Modifiers are roll-specific and are added after this cap.

Attribute, skill, initiative, derived-stat, Social Rating, Physical, Stun, AI Matrix Track, and device Matrix condition-track changes are kept separate from values entered manually. For example, body_modifier:2 adds 2 to Body’s read-only Effects Mod and does not overwrite the user-entered Body Mod. Skill keys such as perception_modifier similarly update that skill’s Effects Mod. Standard Initiative, Initiative Dice, Composure, Judge Intentions, Memory, Lift & Carry, and additional Minor Actions also maintain distinct manual and Effects modifiers.

The four AI attributes use distinct keys: firewall_attribute_modifier, sleaze_attribute_modifier, data_processing_attribute_modifier, and attack_attribute_modifier. These are separate from the Persona/Matrix rating keys named Firewall, Sleaze, Data Processing, and Attack.

pain_tolerance_effect is a supported signed condition modifier. A positive total acts as High Pain Tolerance and reduces the combined Physical and Stun wound penalty by 1. A negative total acts as Low Pain Tolerance and doubles the combined wound penalty. A total of 0 has no effect, and values beyond +1 or -1 do not increase either result. Its Effects total combines with the separate Pain Tolerance selection in Condition Monitor settings.

Augmentations and grades

An augmentation’s Active toggle controls only its Modifications contribution. Essence cost remains applied even while the augmentation is disabled because implantation is a persistent change. Exoware applies its supported Social Rating and Physical Condition Monitor adjustments. Omega-grade Bad Luck is added only to tests that actually use an attribute or skill modified by that Omega-grade augmentation.

Cyberadept Gammaware uses its special Essence multiplier when Cyberadept Gammaware is enabled in Options. Gammaware rows expose their side-effect controls only while Gammaware is selected; an active side effect can apply its own Modifications independently of the augmentation’s base changes.

Unrestricted modifiers

The Options tab contains Enable Unrestricted Modifiers. When disabled, unlisted keys are ignored. When enabled, other attribute names may be changed directly, so use that option carefully and only with known Roll20 attribute names.

The Rebuild Effects button at the bottom of Options clears supported stored modifier targets and reconstructs them from currently active rows. It also clears unrestricted keys that remain present in an existing row, but it cannot discover a key belonging only to a row that was already deleted. Because some legacy modifier keys share storage with manually entered fields, review those fields after rebuilding.

The Options tab also contains Ignore Mod Cap. When enabled, attribute and skill Mod plus Effects Mod totals are no longer limited to +4. Turning it off immediately restores the normal cap.

Situational Modifiers

Situational modifiers represent circumstances that apply to some rolls but not every use of a skill or attribute—for example, a Perception modifier named Visual +2 or an Agility modifier for unstable footing. They are selected at roll time and do not change a skill or attribute’s permanent Mod or Effects Mod.

Creating modifiers

  1. Open the Skills area and select the Modifiers tab beside Skills and Knowledge.
  2. Add a row for each circumstance.
  3. Select the associated skill or attribute, enter a descriptive name, enter its signed dice-pool value, and optionally enter a signed current Edge adjustment.
Perception | Visual | +2 | Edge 0
Agility | Unstable footing | -2 | Edge +1

You can add any number of rows, including multiple modifiers assigned to the same skill or attribute.

Using modifiers

When a supported roll is clicked, the sheet finds every situational modifier assigned to any skill or attribute used by that roll. If matches exist, one combined panel opens with an Apply checkbox for each modifier. A row matches by skill or by attribute; it does not require a particular skill-and-attribute combination.

When Submit is pressed, the Edge values from all checked rows are added together and queued for the resulting roll. The adjustment is applied only after Roll20 accepts any macro-query window and completes the roll. Canceling that window, an attack canceled for lack of ammunition, or a roll blocked by a status does not change Edge. Positive values add current Edge and negative values remove it. Current Edge cannot be reduced below 0 or raised above the sheet’s seven-hex maximum. Extended tests apply the adjustment only when the initial roll completes, not again during later intervals.

Direct attribute and skill rolls, derived tests, Core-tab weapon attacks, Actions, Matrix Actions that require tests, and the Attributes-tab Sprint roll use applicable situational modifiers. Action and Sprint panels also offer Trained, Specialized (+2), or Expertise (+3) when the linked skill has the corresponding specialization or expertise. Actions that allow a choice of skill or attribute refresh the available modifiers when that choice changes.

Options includes Allow Additional Skill Training for custom games. When enabled, each Skill can show a second Specialization after its primary Specialization is filled and a second Expertise after its primary Expertise is filled. Either learned entry can match weapon, spell, Complex Form, Action, Matrix Action, or Sprint training checks, but only one training bonus applies to a roll. A future dedicated Training tab may replace these fixed secondary fields if open-ended training receives sufficient demand.

The roll’s skill rating or attributes, manual Mod, Effects Mod, selected training bonus, wound modifier, general roll modifier, and all checked situational modifiers are combined for the final test. The chat result lists the situational modifiers that were selected.

When the panel appears

The Modifiers toggle in Macro Options controls whether situational modifiers are offered. Direct attribute, skill, weapon, and Matrix Action buttons open the panel only when the toggle is enabled and matching situational modifiers exist; otherwise they roll immediately. Action buttons may still open it to present their skill, attribute, or training choices when no situational modifier is available or the toggle is disabled. The Attributes-tab Sprint button similarly opens for available Athletics specialization or expertise choices.

Specializations and Expertise

Each active skill row provides skill-specific Specialization and Expertise dropdowns. Choose a standard entry for that skill or select Custom to enter another name. Existing values from the legacy text fields are converted automatically: recognized entries select their standard choice, while other entries are preserved as custom text.

A weapon’s Training Type is selected in its Ranged, Melee, or Explosives settings. Spell and Complex Form rows provide equivalent training choices for their supported skills. Standard choices are based on the linked skill, with a Custom field available when needed. An exact Expertise match provides +3; otherwise an exact Specialization match provides +2. A choice that is not learned on the Skills tab provides no bonus. Changing the linked skill, training choice, or learned Specialization or Expertise automatically updates the match.

Roll descriptions and extended tests

Actions, Matrix Actions, Edge options, attributes, and skills provide structured descriptive mouseover text. Direct skill, Action, and rolled Matrix Action results include a Display Description button that sends the canonical description to chat. Matrix Actions that require no test are still buttons; clicking one displays its description directly instead of rolling dice.

Matrix Perception, Matrix Search, and Probe start the sheet’s Extended Test workflow instead of making a basic one-step test. Their mouseover text identifies them as Extended Tests, and Matrix resistance information is retained through every interval.

Defense rolls

Weapon attack results include a Roll Defense button. Select the defending token before pressing it; the defense roll uses the character represented by that token rather than the character that made the attack. The defense options panel can apply choices such as Full Defense and other roll-specific defense adjustments.

Important distinctions

  • Situational modifiers are chosen separately for each roll.
  • They do not write into the skill’s Mod or Effects Mod.
  • Specialization and Expertise bonuses come from learned skill training and are separate from situational modifiers.
  • The temporary checklist is rebuilt whenever a roll panel opens and is cleared when the sheet opens.
  • Untrained use is handled by the linked attribute minus 1 when the character does not possess the required skill.

Gear and Installed Modifications

The Gear section contains four child tabs: Gear, Ammo, Wpn Mods, and Armor Mods. Ordinary gear can apply the sheet-wide Effects modifiers described on the Effects help tab. Weapon Mods and Armor Mods instead attach their bonuses to one selected weapon or armor item.

Ordinary Gear

Each Gear row has an Active power button and a Modifications field. While Active is enabled, the row can use any whitelisted modifier from the Effects help tab, including attribute, skill, initiative, movement, condition-monitor, Social, and Persona modifiers.

The Carried? checkbox in the row settings records whether the character is carrying the item. The Gear list displays True in the Carried column when checked and leaves the column blank when unchecked. Carried is informational and does not enable the item or apply its Modifications; use the Active power button for that.

Use the standard modifier_name:value format and separate multiple entries with commas.

body_modifier:1, perception_modifier:2

A gear row can use its own Rating with rating_num, -rating_num, or rating_num*X. For example, an active Rating 3 item with firewall_modifier:rating_num contributes 3.

Physical, mental, and AI attribute and skill enhancement bonuses from Mod and Effects Mod are subject to the combined +4 cap. Magic and Resonance, along with roll-specific situational modifiers, remain outside that cap.

Ammunition and reloading

The Ammo tab stores ammunition by Category, Load Type, and whether it is Caseless. Custom categories are supported. A ranged weapon uses the same three-part identity, so ammunition is transferred only between matching inventory and weapon entries.

Set a ranged weapon’s Ammo Category in Arms. On Core, select its Load and Caseless state, edit the currently loaded amount if needed, and use Reload to draw matching rounds from inventory up to the weapon’s maximum Ammo. Changing a loaded weapon’s category, load type, or caseless state returns its remaining rounds to the previous matching inventory entry before switching.

Firing from Core expends current ammunition according to the selected firing mode. If a narrow Burst Fire attack has too few rounds, the sheet applies the partial-burst Damage Value and Attack Rating adjustments; one remaining round is treated as Single Shot. Enable Disable Ammo Tracking in Options to prevent attacks from decrementing loaded ammunition. The optional High Strength Reduces Recoil house rule lessens firing-mode AR penalties by 1 at Strength 7 or higher and by 2 at Strength 10 or higher.

Weapon Mods

The Weapon Mods list is shared by ranged and melee weapons. Press Install and choose any weapon on the sheet. The Installed On column identifies both its type and name. Active installed mods contribute their numeric fields and Modifications entries to that weapon only, whether or not the weapon is shown on Core.

The dedicated fields are Pool, Damage, All AR, Close, Near, Medium, Far, and Extreme. All AR applies at every range and combines with the individual range value.

Firing Mode defaults to Any. When a specific mode is selected, that mod contributes only while its installed ranged weapon is using that mode. A mismatch temporarily excludes the bonuses without changing the mod’s Active toggle.

The Modifications box accepts these keys:

pooldicepool damagedv arar_all ar_closear_nearar_mediumar_farar_extreme
pool:1, damage:2, ar_all:-1, ar_close:2

Values in the Modifications box add to values entered in the dedicated fields. Uninstalling a mod removes it from its weapon and turns it off.

Armor Mods

Armor Mods attach to a specific armor item through the Install button. Installed hardware consumes Capacity whether its Active toggle is on or off. DR, resistance, and Social bonuses apply only while the mod is Active.

The dedicated fields are Capacity, DR, Social, Chem, Cold, Electric, and Fire. The Modifications box accepts these keys:

capacitycapacity_used drdefense_rating chemchemical cold elecelectricelectrical firesocial
capacity:2, dr:1, electric:2, fire:1

Text entries add to the dedicated numeric fields. Capacity text values are consumed while installed; all other text bonuses follow the Active toggle.

Weapons on Core

Ranged and melee weapons are configured in Arms but attacks are initiated from Core Combat. Turn on Show on Core for every weapon that should appear there; multiple weapons can be shown and no primary weapon is required. Core uses the selected repeating weapon row directly, including its skill, attribute, training, notes, installed mods, firing mode, and ammunition.

The Explosives section supports grenades, launchers, and other explosive entries. Selecting None for its skill makes the control display the explosive’s details to chat without performing a test.

Matrix devices and programs

Programs are assigned to a specific device with Assign Device. Assignment means Installed; the program’s power toggle separately controls whether it is Running. Running programs consume their configured normal or dedicated Slot Cost from their owner. Slot summaries and warnings remain visible when capacity is exceeded, and GM Override records an approved overage without deleting programs.

Devices provide base Program Slots, a Slot Modifier, Dedicated Slots, Virtual Machine support, and device-specific exceptions. RCCs account for their shared programs and autosofts. Software Emulator supports eligible living-persona programs, while AI inherent or emulated programs use their corresponding slot rules.

Primary Device identifies the main device and defaults Contributes to Persona on. Every device with Contributes to Persona enabled participates in Persona ASDF calculation. Technomancers and AIs fall back to their innate derived Matrix attributes only when no device contributes. AI Optimized Home Device is AI-only, is limited to one device, and includes its Device Rating adjustment.

Syntax and controls

  • Separate entries with commas and use a colon between each key and signed number.
  • Positive and negative integers are supported.
  • Unknown keys are ignored.
  • The power button enables or disables mechanical bonuses without uninstalling the mod.
  • The settings button opens the editable fields; Uninstall removes the current assignment.
